scope: Reviewed natural location and troubleshooting summaries; not an exhaustive spawn simulator.

spawning.answer: Look underwater in lush caves with clay less than five blocks below the spawning space. Blue axolotls come from breeding rather than natural spawning.

spawn_conditions.answer: Check for a lush-caves biome, water and nearby clay below the spawning space. A pond in another biome is not enough. Blue axolotls do not naturally spawn.

spawning.answer: Look below Y=40 in a slime chunk, or in swamps and mangrove swamps at Y=51–69 with light level 7 or less. Swamp spawning depends on the moon: full moons are best, and new moons produce none. In Bedrock, slime-chunk coordinates are the same across world seeds.

spawn_conditions.answer: Underground slime-chunk spawning needs Y below 40 and does not depend on light or weather. Swamp spawning needs Y=51–69, light level 7 or less and a suitable moon phase; none spawn there on a new moon. Leave clear space. In Bedrock, slime-chunk coordinates are the same across world seeds.

spawning.answer: Creepers naturally spawn in dark Overworld areas, excluding mushroom fields, deep dark, rivers, frozen rivers and snowy plains in Bedrock.

spawn_conditions.answer: For ordinary natural spawning, check darkness, a suitable solid surface, space, enabled mob spawning and a difficulty above Peaceful. Bedrock excludes mushroom fields, deep dark, rivers, frozen rivers and snowy plains. Lighting can prevent spawning; it does not remove an existing creeper.

spawning.answer: Look in oceans, rivers and dripstone-cave water. Some ocean ruins generate drowned. Ordinary zombies can also convert after prolonged submersion.

spawn_conditions.answer: Natural spawning needs water with no emitted block light and sky light 7 or less. Bedrock uses surface spawning checks, not Java’s universal below-Y=58 rule. Rivers and dripstone caves have higher rates than oceans. Zombie conversion and ocean-ruin generation are separate sources.

spawning.answer: Phantoms appear above players who have gone a long time without resting. In Bedrock, suitable dark surface spawning locations and access to the sky matter; they are not restricted to Java’s night-only rule.

spawn_conditions.answer: Check prolonged time without resting, open sky above the player, suitable surface spawning locations at light 7 or less, the monster cap and the doInsomnia game rule. Entering a bed resets the rest timer. Bedrock can spawn phantoms during daytime if the other conditions are met.

spawning.answer: Wardens emerge after repeated warnings from naturally generated sculk shriekers, usually in the deep dark. They do not use ordinary dark-floor monster spawning.

spawn_conditions.answer: A player’s warning level must reach four through naturally generated sculk shriekers. The shrieker needs a valid nearby emergence space. Light level does not control this process. A shrieker collected and placed by a player does not summon a warden like a naturally generated one.

spawning.answer: Look around active creaking hearts in pale gardens at night. A heart can also be activated outside that biome in the Overworld with correctly aligned pale oak blocks.

spawn_conditions.answer: At night in the Overworld, an activated creaking heart needs pale oak blocks on opposite sides along its own axis and a valid nearby spawning space. The heart-linked creaking differs from a command-created one; an ordinary dark platform alone does not produce it.

spawning.answer: Find iron golems in villages, or construct one. Bedrock village spawning has bed, villager and working requirements; it does not use Java’s three-panicking-villager setup.

spawn_conditions.answer: A Bedrock village needs at least 20 beds and 10 villagers, all villagers linked to beds, and at least 75% of eligible villagers having worked recently. The village center must be in simulation distance, with a valid unobstructed spawning surface nearby. Three frightened villagers alone are not the Bedrock requirements.

spawning.answer: Find cats in villages and a black cat at a swamp hut. Bedrock village cats depend on claimed beds and the number of cats already in the village.

spawn_conditions.answer: Bedrock villages try to fill a quota of one cat per four claimed beds, up to five cats at 20 or more claimed beds. Existing cats, including babies and tamed visitors, count toward the quota. Provide a valid spawning space near the village center; merely placing unclaimed beds is not enough.

spawning.answer: Wolf coats depend on the biome: pale in taiga, ashen in snowy taiga, black in old growth pine taiga, chestnut in old growth spruce taiga, rusty in sparse jungle, snowy in grove, spotted in savanna plateau, striped in wooded badlands and woods in forest.

spawn_conditions.answer: Check the natural habitat of the coat you want and a suitable surface such as grass, coarse dirt, snow, snow blocks or podzol. A spawn egg’s biome-selected coat does not prove wolves naturally spawn in every biome with that coat. Wolves near biome borders can differ.

spawning.answer: Look in roofed dark Overworld spaces, except the deep dark. In Bedrock, bats can spawn at any height on suitable stone-type blocks with light level 4 or less.

spawn_conditions.answer: Check light level 4 or less, no direct sky exposure, enough air space, and stone, granite, diorite, andesite, tuff or deepslate below. Bats have an ambient population cap; a low cave height alone is not the deciding condition.

spawning.answer: Find bees inside naturally generated bee nests on trees. Flower-rich biomes such as meadows are useful places to search. Growing suitable trees can also produce nests with bees.

spawn_conditions.answer: Bees come with generated nests rather than randomly appearing around a crafted empty beehive. Growing oak, birch or cherry saplings within two blocks of suitable flowers has a chance to produce a populated nest; a single tree is not guaranteed to do so.

spawning.answer: Find bogged on the surface in swamps and mangrove swamps, or from certain trial-chamber spawners.

spawn_conditions.answer: Bedrock natural bogged spawning is surface-only, at light levels 0–7 in swamps or mangrove swamps. A dark underground swamp cave is not the same route. Trial spawners are separate and must have bogged selected as their mob.

spawning.answer: Look for breeze trial spawners in trial-chamber combat rooms, commonly surrounded by chiseled tuff. Breezes do not naturally wander around ordinary caves.

spawn_conditions.answer: Use a breeze-configured trial spawner in a trial-chamber combat room. It needs a valid spawn position with line of sight to the spawner. A normal dark platform or an unrelated trial spawner does not produce breezes.

spawning.answer: Look in Nether fortresses, especially at blaze-spawner platforms. Blazes can also spawn naturally within fortress spawning areas.

spawn_conditions.answer: Blazes require light level 11 or less. Natural fortress spawning depends on the fortress piece or overall fortress bounds; in the larger fortress bounds, Nether bricks are required. Spawner spawning is a separate route, so an ordinary Nether-brick platform outside a fortress is not enough.

spawning.answer: Find witches in dark Overworld areas, swamp huts and raids. Lightning can also turn a villager into a witch.

spawn_conditions.answer: Bedrock witches avoid natural spawning in mushroom fields, deep dark, rivers, frozen rivers and snowy plains. Swamp huts use a particular hardcoded spawning spot, not Java’s whole-hut spawning volume. Raid spawning and lightning conversion are separate routes.

spawning.answer: Look in water at an ocean monument. Bedrock guardian farms use fixed spawning columns tied to the monument.

spawn_conditions.answer: Bedrock guardians use 25 predetermined columns with water-source checks, rather than spawning anywhere across a Java-style monument volume. Removing the monument blocks alone does not remove those spawning positions. Check the column, water and obstructions.

spawning.answer: Each ocean monument generates three elder guardians: one in the top room and one in each wing. They do not naturally respawn.

spawn_conditions.answer: Elder guardians generate with the monument, not through a repeatable dark-water spawning cycle. Once the three are gone, waiting or rebuilding monument blocks will not naturally replace them.

spawning.answer: Look in Nether wastes, soul sand valleys and basalt deltas. Ghasts can spawn at any light level.

spawn_conditions.answer: A ghast needs a solid block beneath its spawn position and about five by five blocks of clear width with four blocks of height. A cramped tunnel will not work. Light is not the deciding restriction; the biome and large clear space matter.

spawning.answer: Find magma cubes in the Nether, especially basalt deltas, and from magma-cube spawners in bastion treasure rooms.

spawn_conditions.answer: Natural magma-cube spawning permits any light level but needs enough clear space without solid or liquid obstructions. Space is checked before the cube’s final size is selected, so a tiny gap is not sufficient just because small cubes exist. Monster spawners are a separate source.

spawning.answer: Look in Nether fortresses. In Bedrock, the Wither can also produce wither skeletons during its fight on Normal or Hard difficulty.

spawn_conditions.answer: Natural wither-skeleton spawning needs a fortress spawning area, light level 0–7 and enough room for the tall mob. Within overall fortress bounds but outside individual fortress pieces, Nether-brick flooring matters. A Nether-brick platform outside a fortress is not sufficient.

spawning.answer: Find piglins in Nether wastes, crimson forests and generated bastion remnants.

spawn_conditions.answer: Bedrock natural piglins need light level 7 or less in their eligible Nether biomes. They do not naturally spawn on Nether wart blocks or magma blocks. Bastion generation is another source; ordinary piglins and piglin brutes have different replenishment rules.

spawning.answer: Find piglin brutes in generated bastion-remnant rooms. Those original brutes do not naturally respawn.

spawn_conditions.answer: Piglin brutes are generated with bastions and do not replenish through ordinary natural spawning. Darkness, waiting or adding gold does not make a cleared bastion grow new brutes.

spawning.answer: Find hoglins in crimson forests and certain bastion areas, especially hoglin stables. Crimson-forest hoglins can respawn over time.

spawn_conditions.answer: Natural hoglins can spawn at any light level in crimson forests. In Bedrock, Nether wart blocks and shroomlights are unsuitable spawning surfaces. Leave adequate space; bastion-generated hoglins are a separate source.

spawning.answer: Endermen occur in the Overworld, Nether and End. Warped forests are especially useful in the Nether, and endermen are common in the End.

spawn_conditions.answer: Endermen need a suitable solid surface and three empty blocks above. They need darkness in the Overworld and End, or light 7 or less in the Nether. Bedrock Overworld exclusions include mushroom fields, deep dark, rivers, frozen rivers and snowy plains.

spawning.answer: An endermite can appear when a player’s thrown ender pearl lands. In Bedrock it appears at the pearl’s landing site.

spawn_conditions.answer: A player-thrown ender pearl has a 5% chance to produce an endermite when it lands. A dark platform does not naturally generate them. Endermites disappear after about two minutes unless named with a name tag.

spawning.answer: Find silverfish in infested blocks, stronghold End-portal-room spawners and certain trial spawners. The Infested effect can also produce them.

spawn_conditions.answer: Breaking an infested block without Silk Touch can release silverfish. Stronghold silverfish spawners need light level 11 or less. Trial spawners must be configured for silverfish; ordinary darkness alone is not their natural source.

spawning.answer: Find shulkers on End-city walls and End ships on the outer End islands. They generate with those structures.

spawn_conditions.answer: End-city generation supplies the original shulkers; an empty city does not normally refill by waiting. Additional shulkers can come from special shulker-bullet duplication mechanics, not ordinary animal breeding or a dark End platform.

spawning.answer: Brush suspicious sand in warm ocean ruins to look for sniffer eggs, then hatch an egg. Sniffers do not naturally spawn as wandering adults.

spawn_conditions.answer: A sniffer must hatch from an egg; breeding existing sniffers can also produce eggs. For the first egg, use archaeology in warm ocean ruins. Waiting in a biome or building a dark platform does not make adult sniffers naturally appear.

spawning.answer: Look on sandy beaches, excluding snowy beaches and stony shores. In Bedrock, natural turtles spawn at Y=60–67.

spawn_conditions.answer: Check an eligible beach, sand and Y=60–67 for natural Bedrock turtles. Breeding is different: a turtle returns to its home beach to lay eggs, so a random new sand pen may not be its chosen nesting place.

spawning.answer: Frogs naturally spawn in swamps and mangrove swamps. To obtain a cold frog, raise a tadpole in a cold biome.

spawn_conditions.answer: Ordinary natural spawning is in swamps and mangrove swamps. A tadpole’s growth biome determines its adult frog color; moving an adult frog does not recolor it. Spawn eggs and biome-border cases are different from normal natural habitats.

spawning.answer: Look on snowy slopes, jagged peaks and frozen peaks, on surfaces such as stone, gravel, packed ice and snow blocks.

spawn_conditions.answer: Use the correct mountain biome and a suitable surface. Natural spawning after world generation is less common than the original groups. A snowy mountain-looking build in a different biome does not create the required habitat.

spawning.answer: Look in jungles, especially bamboo jungles. Pandas naturally appear on grass blocks rather than podzol.

spawn_conditions.answer: Check a jungle biome, grass blocks and at least two blocks of space above. Natural pandas are rare. Breeding has a separate nearby-bamboo requirement; placing bamboo in another biome does not make that biome a natural panda habitat.

spawning.answer: Look in jungles, bamboo jungles and sparse jungles in Bedrock, on grass blocks.

spawn_conditions.answer: Bedrock ocelots can naturally spawn in all jungle types at light level 7 or above. Grass blocks matter. Do not apply Java’s sparse-jungle exclusion to Bedrock.

spawning.answer: Look in jungles, bamboo jungles and sparse jungles in Bedrock, around grass, logs and leaves.

spawn_conditions.answer: Natural parrots require eligible jungle habitats. Sparse jungle is valid in Bedrock. Parrots cannot breed, so pairing two with seeds will not produce babies.

spawning.answer: Look in completely dark underground water from Y=-64 to Y=30 in Bedrock, outside the deep dark.

spawn_conditions.answer: Check light level 0, Y=-64 through 30, water and a solid roof so the location counts as underground. Ordinary surface squid use a different spawning route. Deep dark is excluded.

spawning.answer: Look in ocean and river water. Bedrock squid are surface water spawns rather than underground cave spawns.

spawn_conditions.answer: A Bedrock squid spawn must not have a solid or spawnable block above the location. Do not automatically apply Java’s Y=50–63 range. A roofed tank can fail even though it contains water.

spawning.answer: Look in ocean water between Y=50 and Y=64, excluding cold and frozen oceans.

spawn_conditions.answer: Natural dolphins need an eligible ocean biome and Y=50–64. A river, cold ocean or frozen ocean is not the same habitat. Breeding dolphins with fish does not create new dolphins.

spawning.answer: Look in warm, lukewarm and deep lukewarm oceans, mangrove swamps and lush-cave water.

spawn_conditions.answer: In Bedrock ocean spawning, check Y=50–64 and the surface-water conditions. Lush-cave aquifers can work at other heights but must count as underground. Tropical fish do not naturally spawn in every pond merely because it contains water.

spawning.answer: In Bedrock, look in warm oceans. They are rarer there than tropical fish.

spawn_conditions.answer: Bedrock pufferfish require warm-ocean surface water, with suitable player distance around 12–32 blocks. Do not substitute Java’s lukewarm/deep-lukewarm spawning list or roof over the spawning water.

spawning.answer: Look in cages at pillager outposts and jail cells in woodland mansions. The original allays generate with those structures; not every cage or cell contains them.

spawn_conditions.answer: Allays do not refill a cleared structure through ordinary natural spawning. Search another eligible structure or duplicate an existing allay with an amethyst shard while it dances to a jukebox.

spawning.answer: Look in savanna, savanna plateau, windswept savanna, badlands, wooded badlands and eroded badlands.

spawn_conditions.answer: Bedrock armadillos need light level 7 or more in their eligible savanna or badlands habitats. A warm climate alone does not make every desert a valid armadillo biome.

spawning.answer: Look in ocean biomes between Y=38 and Y=58, usually in small groups.

spawn_conditions.answer: Natural nautiluses need ocean water in the Y=38–58 range. A shallow river is not their natural habitat. Zombie nautiluses use a separate drowned-jockey route.

spawning.answer: Look for trident-wielding adult drowned riding zombie nautiluses in oceans and dripstone caves. Warm-ocean examples have the coral appearance.

spawn_conditions.answer: An eligible trident-wielding adult drowned outside river and frozen-river biomes has a chance to generate mounted on a zombie nautilus. It is not made by leaving an ordinary nautilus underwater. Structure-generated drowned are another eligible route.

spawning.answer: Waterlog a dried ghast for about 20 minutes to obtain a ghastling, then let it grow into a happy ghast.

spawn_conditions.answer: Happy ghasts do not use ordinary hostile-ghast spawning. Keep a dried ghast waterlogged until it becomes a ghastling. Snowballs speed up the ghastling’s growth, but two happy ghasts do not breed.

spawning.answer: Look in sulfur caves, where large sulfur cubes naturally spawn at any light level.

spawn_conditions.answer: Check the sulfur-caves biome and a suitable clear spawning space. Darkness is not required. Small sulfur cubes come from a large cube splitting and can grow; they are not the ordinary naturally spawned form.

spawning.answer: Obtain a mule by breeding a horse with a donkey. Mules do not naturally spawn in a biome.

spawn_conditions.answer: Breed a horse and donkey rather than waiting for a wild mule. Mules cannot breed with each other.

spawning.answer: A hoglin becomes a zoglin after spending 15 seconds outside the Nether. Zoglins are not a normal biome-spawning herd.

spawn_conditions.answer: Conversion requires a hoglin outside the Nether for 15 seconds. Lighting a platform or breeding zoglins does not create more of them.

Camels can appear in deserts, including the original camel generated in a non-abandoned desert village. Clearing or rebuilding a village does not regenerate that original camel. Ordinary natural spawning and the village-generated camel are separate sources.

Bedrock camel husks use desert monster spawning and appear with riders, not as ordinary passive desert camels. They do not naturally spawn in Peaceful. Do not apply Java’s exact husk-pack chance to Bedrock.

Mineshaft cave-spider spawners require darkness and usable spawning space. Certain trial spawners can also select cave spiders. Natural cave spiders replace ordinary spiders in sulfur caves; an ordinary dark cave in another biome is not the same route.

Bedrock natural chickens need grass blocks and light level 7 or more in an eligible biome. Snowy plains, meadows, cherry groves, mangrove swamps and pale gardens are excluded. Egg hatching and breeding are separate ways to obtain chickens.

Bedrock cod use surface water in normal, cold, frozen and lukewarm oceans and their deep variants, around 12–32 blocks from the player. A roof or spawnable layer above can block the surface spawning check; a river is not their ordinary natural habitat.

Create a copper golem with a copper block and a carved pumpkin or jack o’lantern, placing the pumpkin last. Oxidation and wax states of the starting block have their own effects. A dark platform or ordinary copper ore does not naturally generate one.

Natural cows need a well-lit grass block, two blocks of space above and an eligible grassy biome. Snowy plains, meadows, cherry groves, mangrove swamps and pale gardens are excluded. Village-generated animals, breeding and shearing a mooshroom are separate routes.

Natural Bedrock donkeys occur in plains, meadows and savannas. A meadow is valid even though it is not an ordinary cow habitat. Breeding requires existing compatible animals; it is separate from waiting for wild donkeys.

The first dragon is associated with entering the End. To resummon it after defeat, use four End crystals, one at the center of each side of the exit portal. A dark platform or a random crystal arrangement away from that portal does not resummon it.

Mansion evokers generate once in particular upper-floor rooms and do not refill after being killed. Another source is a raid on Normal or Hard, starting at wave five. An Easy raid or a cleared mansion is not a repeatable evoker-spawning area.

Red foxes naturally occur in taigas, old growth pine and spruce taigas and dappled forests; snow foxes occur in snowy taigas and groves. Moving a fox or placing snow does not recolor it or change the actual biome.

Natural horses occur in plains and savannas, with some also generated in village animal areas. Coats and markings do not each require a different biome. Donkeys, mules and undead horses have different sources.

Bedrock husks naturally use desert surface spawning, replacing many ordinary zombies. A dark underground desert tunnel is not the same surface route. Monster-spawner or trial-spawner encounters should be treated separately.

Natural llamas require grass blocks, light above 7 and eligible hills or savanna habitats. Bedrock includes regular and windswept savannas as well as savanna plateaus. Trader llamas arrive with wandering traders rather than being ordinary wild herds.

Natural red mooshrooms require mushroom fields and mycelium. Brown mooshrooms do not naturally spawn: use lightning conversion or the rare opposite-color offspring from breeding two matching mooshrooms. Ordinary cows and red mushrooms do not combine into a mooshroom.

Bedrock parched naturally spawn on the desert surface at night, replacing some skeletons. Riders in camel-husk or spider-jockey encounters are another route. A random underground skeleton farm is not automatically a parched farm.

Natural pigs use grass blocks in eligible grassy Overworld biomes. Snowy plains, meadows, mangrove swamps and pale gardens are excluded, but cherry groves can have pigs. Natural pigs are not born with saddles; equipment and breeding are separate.

Pillagers have different sources: outposts, patrols and raids. Bedrock patrols can start after five and a half in-game days and use light 0–7. Bedrock outpost spawning is tied to particular positions; do not copy a Java whole-volume outpost platform without checking the Bedrock positions.

Look in eligible frozen and snowy biomes rather than any place with player-placed snow. Bedrock includes additional frozen river and mountain habitats. Polar bears cannot be bred with fish, so feeding them does not create cubs.

Natural rabbit coats are biome-dependent: gold in deserts, white forms in snowy habitats, and brown, black or salt forms in eligible forest/taiga/meadow habitats. Bedrock also includes frozen aquatic habitats. Spawn-egg colors do not prove natural spawning in every biome.
Ravagers come from raids beginning at wave three, not ordinary dark-platform spawning. Riders depend on the raid wave and difficulty. Bedrock raids do not have Java’s extra-wave system.

Salmon use suitable river and ocean water, not every player-made pond. Their size variants are separate from the biome requirement. Check the water biome and surface spawning conditions rather than assuming a roofed tank will work.

Natural sheep need an eligible biome and suitable grassy spawning area. Their naturally likely wool colors vary by biome; dyeing an existing sheep is separate from natural spawning. A spawn egg can produce appearances that are not proof of wild spawning at that location.

Ordinary skeletons need an eligible dark spawning surface and enough space. Monster rooms and trial spawners are separate sources. Desert and snowy-biome replacement mobs are not simply skeleton coats, and Nether fortress or soul-sand-valley spawning has different context.

Natural skeleton trap horses are associated with thunderstorm lightning. Channeling-trident lightning and lightning directed to a lightning rod do not produce traps. A normal horse struck by lightning is not the recipe for a skeleton horse.

Create one using two snow blocks and a carved pumpkin or jack o’lantern, with the pumpkin placed last. Ordinary snow layers or an uncarved pumpkin do not substitute. It does not naturally spawn just because the biome is snowy.

Natural spiders need a suitable dark surface and enough clear width. Bedrock excludes mushroom fields, deep dark, rivers, frozen rivers and snowy plains; sulfur caves replace ordinary spider spawns with cave spiders. Spawner encounters are a separate route.

Strays naturally occur in eligible snowy and frozen biomes. Another route is keeping an ordinary skeleton in powder snow until it converts; bogged and parched do not use that conversion. Certain trial spawners can also spawn strays.

Striders naturally spawn on lava with air above in Nether biomes. A dry platform does not provide their usual spawning medium. In Bedrock their animal population cap is shared with hoglins, so other animals can affect availability.
Tadpoles hatch from frogspawn laid by breeding frogs. A pond without frogspawn does not spontaneously produce tadpoles, and their eventual frog color depends on where they grow up.
Two trader llamas attempt to appear with a wandering trader and are leashed to it. They are not a separately replenishing wild llama herd. Space around the trader matters to those attempts.

Vexes are summoned by an evoker’s attack, not by normal dark-floor spawning. An evoker needs usable nearby summoning positions. Evoker-summoned vexes have a limited lifetime; spawn eggs and commands are different.

Villagers originally generate with villages and igloo basements. Empty beds or rebuilt village houses do not spontaneously create replacement villagers. Use breeding existing villagers or curing zombie villagers; babies need a breeding setup, not ordinary hostile-mob spawning conditions.

Mansion vindicators generate once and do not refill by waiting. Raids provide another source. A dark mansion-shaped building outside the actual generated structure does not create a natural vindicator farm.

Wandering traders attempt to spawn near players in the Overworld; Bedrock can also try near a claimed village bell. Their appearance is random, not guaranteed on demand. A workstation does not turn a normal villager into a wandering trader.

Summon the Wither using four soul sand or soul soil blocks and three wither skeleton skulls in the Wither construction arrangement, placing a skull last and leaving the required spaces clear. It does not naturally appear in a Nether biome, and Peaceful prevents the fight.

Natural zombies need a suitable dark solid spawning surface and two blocks of height, even for babies. Bedrock excludes mushroom fields, deep dark, rivers, frozen rivers and snowy plains. Desert husks, drowned conversion and zombie-villager generation are separate mechanics.

Natural zombie horsemen require grass in eligible plains, savanna or snowy-plains habitats, suitable darkness and a difficulty allowing monsters. They arrive as a zombie rider and horse, not ordinary passive horse herds. Snow blocks can prevent the grass-based spawning route.

Zombified piglins can appear naturally in eligible Nether areas, from Overworld Nether portals, or from conversions such as piglin zombification and lightning hitting a pig. They do not naturally spawn in Peaceful. A mob travelling through a portal is different from a portal generating one.

Zombie villagers can occur during ordinary zombie spawning, in abandoned villages and igloo basements, or when villagers are killed by eligible zombies. Infection chance is 0% on Easy, 50% on Normal and 100% on Hard. A bed alone does not generate one.

Villagers originally generate with villages and igloo basements. Empty beds or rebuilt village houses do not spontaneously create replacement villagers. Use breeding existing villagers or curing zombie villagers; babies need a breeding setup, not ordinary hostile-mob spawning conditions.

Zombie villagers can occur during ordinary zombie spawning, in abandoned villages and igloo basements, or when villagers are killed by eligible zombies. Infection chance is 0% on Easy, 50% on Normal and 100% on Hard. A bed alone does not generate one.
